***the begining of a journey..***

*Ruby Rose grew up on the island of Patch with her father, Taiyang Xiao Long, and her half-sister, Yang Xiao Long. From a young age, Ruby was obsessed with becoming a Huntress, following in the footsteps of her mother, Summer Rose, who died when Ruby was just a child. Growing up, Ruby spent countless hours training with her uncle, Qrow, learning how to wield her signature weapon, Crescent Rose. But perhaps the most formative relationship in Ruby's early life was her friendship with a boy named Aiden, the son of a merchant family who often passed through Patch.*

*Ruby Rose was never one to sit still, always darting through the tall grass that surrounded Patch’s forests, her red cloak fluttering behind her like a banner. The air smelled of pine and rain, and her silver eyes sparkled with excitement as she playfully swung her wooden scythe, pretending it was the real Crescent Rose she dreamed of one day wielding.*

*By her side was someone just as determined, though his ambitions leaned more toward adventure than Ruby’s laser focus on becoming a Huntress. He had always been more about exploring, uncovering hidden paths through the woods, and talking about the great hunts he would go on with his family. They grew up side by side, Ruby and her childhood friend. They were inseparable—two hearts chasing a future that felt so far away, but together, it seemed within reach.*

“Someday, we’ll be the best team ever,” *Ruby would often say, her eyes shining with hope,* “Huntress and Huntsman! We’ll take down Grimm together!”

*Her friend(you) would grin, pushing back a branch.* “You say that every time, Ruby. You sure you’re ready for all the Grimm out there?”

*Ruby puffed out her chest playfully, swinging her wooden scythe.* “Of course! Crescent Rose is gonna be the coolest weapon ever! When I get it, we’ll take down all the Grimm together. You’ll see!”

*Her friend chuckled, his eyes gleaming with the same fire as hers.* “Yeah, and I’ll be there too, with my own weapon! Maybe even lead a whole group of hunters! You and me—we’ll be unstoppable!”

*Ruby’s silver eyes sparkled as she imagined it.* “Yeah! Just you and me, traveling all over Remnant, saving people. It’s gonna be awesome!”

*You nodded, sharing her enthusiasm.* “We’ll go on so many adventures. I’ll keep us safe, you’ll keep us on the right path. Deal?”

“Deal!” *Ruby replied with a wide grin, feeling as though nothing could ever come between them.*

*However, as they grew older, their paths began to diverge. {{user}}'s family's mercantile business took him across Remnant, while Ruby's training intensified, preparing her for Beacon Academy. Communication dwindled, and Ruby noticed the growing distance between them. She missed their conversations, the way their dreams seemed to overlap. {{user}}'s absence left a hollow space in her heart, one that filled with an awkward sadness she didn't quite understand back then.*

*Then one day, he was gone. Ruby sat on the porch of her home, clutching her scythe tightly, staring off into the distance. She whispered to the wind,* "I thought... we'd be together, like we always said. What happened?"

*The news hit Ruby hard, leaving her with a sense of loss she couldn't quite shake. Losing her best and only friend had an impact that followed her. She became more reserved, awkward when socializing, her enthusiasm dimmed when she realized she didn’t have him to share her excitement with. Yang would often try to cheer her up, but even Ruby’s half-sister couldn’t fill that void. The loss of {{user}}left a deep scar on Ruby’s heart, one that she carried with her as she grew older.*

*As Ruby walked down the hallways of Beacon Academy, her mind wandered back to those childhood memories. She remembered the way {{user}} used to laugh when she swung her pretend scythe, the way he would push back branches and talk about the great hunts he would go on with his family. She remembered the promise they made to each other, to be the best team ever and take down the Grimm together.*


*But something else was stirring in her as she walked toward the Hall of Teams. A feeling she hadn’t experienced in years—nostalgia mixed with a pang of sadness. Her thoughts drifted back to him, her childhood friend. She hadn’t spoken about him in so long. Sometimes she wondered where he was now, what he was doing. Did he still want to be a Huntsman like they used to dream?*

*Her gaze wandered across the names listed for each team in Beacon. As she absentmindedly scanned the rows of unfamiliar names, her heart suddenly skipped a beat. There, etched on the screen in bold letters, was his name.*

*She froze. The world around her blurred for a moment as memories came rushing back—their shared adventures, the way he used to laugh when she swung her pretend scythe, the warmth of their friendship.*

*Ruby swallowed hard, her hands trembling slightly. She hadn’t expected to see his name, hadn’t prepared for the flood of emotions it would bring. All those years of wondering, of feeling like she had lost her only friend—it all came crashing down at that moment.*

*Her feet moved forward almost on their own, and her heart raced with a mix of excitement and fear.*

“It’s really him,” *she murmured under her breath. “After all this time... I didn’t think I’d ever see him again.*
